triples.evidence: The blob store only gets the bytes to the tool; [splats.md](splats.md) covers what the server does about it
A 50 MiB stream of zeros compressed to a few kilobytes is refused (Confirmed, tests).
The review that found this measured 3.8 GB for a 250 MiB blob; it is now refused at once (peak 101 MB, Confirmed).

A tool call on a blob costs about 15 times the decoded size in peak process memory (a 60 MiB scene: 1041 MB peak from a 100 MB baseline, Confirmed), outside `MEM_BYTES`, which is why `X3D_MCP_TOOL_MAX_BYTES` exists
A call decodes its document before it queues for the heavy-job lock, so concurrent calls are admitted only while the decoded text they hold stays within twice that limit

libxml2 refuses a start tag over 10 MB, so a splat scene stored as one huge attribute cannot be parsed, and the XSD check gives an "Internal error" on very large scenes. The blob store only gets the bytes to the tool; [splats.md](splats.md) covers what the server does about it (a "not checkable at this size" verdict, and `splat_chunk`
[splats.md](splats.md) covers what the server does about it (a "not checkable at this size" verdict, and `splat_chunk`, which cuts a splat file into pieces that validate).
